title: 420 Feds Invade Humboldt, But The Secret Was Out Weeks Ago. All U-Hauls Rented. Only Going After “Corporate” – Not Medical – Growers?

content_html_sanitized:
Analysis by Richard Cowan 

Yesterday, the Feds invaded Humboldt County with something like 450 – I couldn’t resist the 420 – people from various agencies, and actually managed to seize a number of plants despite there having been warnings on local blogs and even Craig’s List for over a week. So far there have been no arrests, but that may change. 

The Feds gave themselves away by renting virtually all of the hotel rooms in the area. Humboldt is about as marijuana-friendly as anywhere in California, which is saying a lot, so word spread quickly. As a consequence, it has been impossible to find an available rental truck for the last week, as growers moved their plants and/or dismantled their grows. 

Interestingly, the Feds are emphasizing that they are not going after medical grows, even though they say there is no such thing as medical marijuana. 

See 

Guess Who Said , “The decrease in the abuse of cannabis among youth in the United States may be offset by an increase in the abuse of prescription drugs.” Iron Law Of Prohibition" &. Czar's Strategy 3 

and links 

Recently, I wrote about the blowback against marijuana growing in Mendocino County, which is Humboldt’s neighbor to the south. (The anti-marijuana Proposition B did finally pass narrowly after all the votes were counted.) 

See 

Mendocino and Our “Needle Park” Problem. When a Local Problem Has International Implications. Who Lost The Sheriff? Whose Business Is It? 

Marijuana growing is an even bigger business in Humboldt and even the locals who are anti-prohibitionists are bothered by some of the problems that are the result of black market growers. These problems are ultimately caused by prohibition, but they are real, nonetheless. 

For example, the local fire department estimates that half of all the residential fires are in badly wired grow houses. Homeowners have had their property seriously damaged by renters who are incompetent growers. 

These real dangers create political problems for the cannabis community, and the narks are more than willing to take advantage of the situation. 

Last year, over 350,000 plants were seized in Humboldt (population 128,000), up from just over 100,000 in 2006. By comparison, in 2006, the last year for which numbers are available, approximately 1,749,057 plants were seized in all of Canada (population 33

million.) 

(There were more than twice as many (3,846,017) plants seized in California (population 36 million) as in Canada in 2006. 

The problem for everyone in Humboldt, including the most ardent prohibitionists, is that marijuana is a major part of the local economy. As in Mendocino, logging and fishing are almost dead, and they are too isolated to draw new industries. While some homes have been damaged by bad growers, housing prices have been sustained by indoor growing while prices elsewhere in the state have collapsed. 

Another perverse effect of the raids… A friend who knows the area tells me that the narks passed several meth labs on the way to bust grow-ops. 

See 

Meth and Marijuana. Now: How the Narks Created Crank in Canada. The Iron Law of Drug Prohibition. The Inescapable Economics Of Contraband. 

and links 

Thus far only about 10,000 plants have been seized, so it remains to be seen how great the impact of these raids will be on the total cannabis supply. However, many more plants may have been destroyed by growers as a precautionary measure. Consequently, it is possible that prices will rise sharply in the months ahead. The outdoor crops in many areas of California have been hurt by the severe drought, while to the north in Washington State and BC, heavy rains are the problem. 

Clubs in the Bay Area and in LA are apt to be paying much more for their supplies in the next few months. Of course, increasing the profits for growers will encourage more people to get in the business, and so it goes. 

As levies fail on the Mississippi and its tributaries, and forest fires burn out of control in Humboldt and in much of California, the feds are spending millions of dollars to make everyone’s problems worse.

How Bob Barr Can Mainstream the Marijuana Issue. He Should Talk about The Dutch Experience As Concrete Proof that Cannabis Prohibition Is A Counterproductive Fraud.
